layers.name: UI / Routes
layers.summary: Next.js App Router pages and layouts organised into four route groups: (lobby) public storefront, (auth) sign-in/sign-up flows, (checkout) cart and payment, (dashboard) seller/account management. Global providers live in the root layout.

layers.name: Server Actions
layers.summary: Server-only functions in src/lib/actions/ mutate the database. They always return { data, error } — never throw to the caller. Error strings are produced by getErrorMessage() from src/lib/handle-error.ts.

layers.name: Data Layer
layers.summary: PostgreSQL accessed through Drizzle ORM (postgres-js driver). Schema defines 13 tables. Read queries live in src/lib/queries/ and use unstable_cache. Helpers takeFirst/takeFirstOrThrow replace array indexing.

layers.name: Auth
layers.summary: Clerk handles authentication. Middleware protects only /dashboard(.*); all other routes are public. Signed-out users hitting /dashboard are redirected to /signin.

layers.name: External Services
layers.summary: Six third-party services: Stripe (payments/subscriptions), Clerk (identity), UploadThing (file storage on utfs.io CDN), Upstash Redis (caching/rate-limiting), Resend (transactional email), Loglib (analytics). All credentials validated at startup by @t3-oss/env-nextjs.

layers.name: Content
layers.summary: MDX blog posts processed by Contentlayer from src/content/; types generated into .contentlayer/generated (gitignored). The withContentlayer wrapper integrates with Next.js build.

evidence.note: build script: contentlayer build && next build

edges.label: Clerk SDK calls Clerk cloud API
Upstash Redis used for query caching and rate-limiting
Contentlayer-generated types consumed by blog pages
